text.p: These are the main stories in Estonian newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Reform Party has issued an ultimatum to government partner the Coalition Party, threatening to leave the coalition unless a cooperation deal with the opposition Centre Party is cancelled.
- Trade union leader Raivo Paavo warned about a possible conflict in the northeastern town of Narva if a wage dispute at the huge Kreenholm textile mill is not solved.
- A trade union activist at Kreenholm has threatened to go on hunger strike unless wages are raised.
- Swedish ambassador Katarina Brodin and the wife of President Lennart Meri, Helle Meri, opened a nursery in the western town of Haapsalu.

- The newspaper comments about an increasing Russian influence in Estonia and a process of "finlandisation" as the Centre Party has returned to power in Tallinn and will probably be involved in the national government.
- The newspaper has an interview with Uno Laur, the Estonian chairman of the commission investigation the Estonia disaster.

- Lithuanian aviation authorities have asked Estonian Air, majority-owned by Maersk, to cut its Tallinn-Vilnius flights to three a day. The reason given is the larger capacity of the planes currently used.

- Estonian and Danish transport ministers are to meet next Thursday to discuss the flights row between Estonia and Scandinavian Airlines. The summer flight schedule between Tallinn and Copenhagen has been extended until Friday.
